title: Lubricating Oil Pump
model_title: Lubricating Oil Pump Console (Main + Standby, API 614 Style)

introduction.definition: A lubricating-oil system (console) supplies clean, cooled oil at controlled pressure to the bearings of turbines, compressors and large pumps. Main and standby pumps — here three-screw pumps — draw from a reservoir and deliver through twin coolers, duplex filters and pressure control valves; API 614 governs special-purpose systems.
key_points: Built from: Three Screw Pump (20) or External Gear Pump (17)
Main + standby with auto-start on low pressure
Duplex filters and coolers switchable on-line

classification.configuration: Lube-oil console with main + standby rotary screw pumps

introduction.summary: A lubricating-oil console supplies clean, cool oil at controlled pressure to the bearings (and often seals) of large machines such as turbines, compressors and big pumps. Oil is drawn from a reservoir by a main pump; an identical standby pump starts automatically if header pressure falls. Duplex filters and twin coolers can be switched over while running for maintenance, and a pressure-control valve spills excess oil back to the tank. Positive-displacement screw or gear pumps are used because they give steady flow regardless of oil viscosity.

script.narration: This module introduces the Lubricating Oil Pump.
A lubricating-oil system (console) supplies clean, cooled oil at controlled pressure to the bearings of turbines, compressors and large pumps.
Main and standby pumps — here three-screw pumps — draw from a reservoir and deliver through twin coolers, duplex filters and pressure control valves; API 614 governs special-purpose systems.
Typical applications include steam and gas turbines; centrifugal compressors; large pumps and gearboxes; alumina refinery turbine-generators and blowers.
The cutaway reveals the internal construction: Main Lube-Oil Pump (Three-Screw), Main Pump – Power Rotor, Main Pump – Idler Rotor, Main Pump – Idler Rotor.
The exploded view separates every component so each one can be tapped for its function, material and failure modes.
Next, watch the operation tutorial to see how it works.

script.narration: Maintenance essentials for the Lubricating Oil Pump.
Check header pressure and filter ΔP.
Switch filters and change elements.
Oil analysis.
Inspect pumps and coolers.
Watch for low header pressure trip: turbine trip. Common cause: pump wear, filter blockage.
Watch for water in oil: milky oil. Common cause: cooler leak.
Record every inspection so trends — vibration, temperature, leakage and performance — can be compared over time.
